principles: Confidence must never be manufactured from incomplete identity.
Command execution truth and current coverage truth are separate facts that compose into the overall verdict.
Metadata-only progress should not create repeated expensive work.
One shared lineage primitive should govern trusted metadata descendants.
Observability must distinguish execution from reuse and explain every refusal.
drivers: Eliminate measured identical-command validation waste after evidence refresh.
Preserve fail-closed safety across all validation sources and modes.
Allow current coverage repair to consume an already successful command execution.
Avoid new metadata churn and self-invalidating cache behavior.
Keep DONE-specific proof semantics separate from routine validation.

options.name: A: Shared lineage plus separate commandExecution identity
pros: Handles B-19ca coverage-only FAIL without rerunning commands
cons: Requires evidence schema extension and migration-by-execution
Needs broad table-driven tests and a subsystem decision doc

options.name: B: Reuse only prior overall PASS on material and story hashes
cons: Unsound when commands, config, environment, entrypoint, focus/profile or policy change

options.name: C: Separate HEAD-keyed cache artifact
cons: Cache writes can create more HEAD drift
Still needs a separate command-versus-coverage model

chosen: A: Shared lineage plus separate commandExecution identity
rationale: Option A directly models the evidence observed in B-19ca: commandExecution can be PASS while the old overall verdict is FAIL because coverage is stale. A later request may reuse that command PASS only after it recomputes current coverage as complete and matches the complete plan, effective-environment, mode, policy, material, story-file and lineage identity under the lock. Mutable verificationEvidence records are excluded from the command identity so repairing them does not invalidate execution; required intent definitions and workflow policy remain bound. A dedicated subsystem decision document is the canonical contract.

preMortem.scenario: A changed command, effective environment or validate config incorrectly reuses an old command PASS.
preMortem.trigger: Identity omits normalized command args, cwd, shell, timeout, explicit env overlay, effective environment digest, source or entrypoint digest.
preMortem.consequence: Validation reports PASS without executing a behaviorally changed plan.
preMortem.mitigation: Canonicalize and hash the full resolved plan and effective child environment; persist only hashes; add one-dimension-at-a-time mismatch tests.

preMortem.scenario: A coverage-only old FAIL is reused even though current coverage remains incomplete.
preMortem.trigger: Eligibility trusts stored overall/result or stored coverage instead of recomputing the current checklist policy.
preMortem.consequence: Missing verification evidence is laundered into PASS.
preMortem.mitigation: Require stored commandExecution.status=PASS but always recompute current coverage and require missingRequired=0 before reuse.

preMortem.scenario: Metadata-only validation commits cause an infinite reuse/write/drift loop.
preMortem.trigger: The reused path rewrites test-evidence or auto-commits a disposition artifact.
preMortem.consequence: Every reuse moves HEAD and invalidates itself.
preMortem.mitigation: Return reused disposition without writing; assert artifact bytes and HEAD unchanged.

preMortem.scenario: HEAD changes between reuse check and return.
preMortem.trigger: Concurrent metadata or source write occurs after the first read.
preMortem.consequence: A PASS for one tree is returned for another.
preMortem.mitigation: Decide under the validation lock, read HEAD before and after, and execute on drift.

preMortem.scenario: Focused or fallback validation is mistaken for full configured validation.
preMortem.trigger: Identity omits source kind, focus/full/profile or entrypoint digest.
preMortem.consequence: A narrower PASS satisfies a broader request.
preMortem.mitigation: Bind mode and source-specific fields; add cross-mode/source refusal tests.

preMortem.scenario: Legacy or malformed evidence crashes or reuses accidentally.
preMortem.mitigation: Missing or malformed fields produce named refusal and real execution.
